arr.name: All Rights Reserved
arr.title: [ NO MILK RECORDS | ALL RIGHTS RESERVED ] marlboro, nj [ RIP ]
bio: When originally formed in 2000, this band was nothing more than 4 aspiring musicians with big dreams. Since then, ALL RIGHTS RESERVED has matured into one of the hardest working bands in the country. With numerous tours of the United States under their belts, they have left a trail of impressed fans in every state they have conquered. Sharing the stage with acts like All American Rejects, and MxPx, in addition to 3 performances at NJs Skate and Surf Festival has created an almost, telephone-like word of mouth hype throughout the country. Nine straight months of touring to support their debut EP, Remind Me To Burn These Pages (released 11-25-03 on Pumpkineater Records) has been both an effective advertising campaign as well as a highly positive marketing plan. With over 5,000 copies of the EP sold worldwide, ALL RIGHTS RESERVED was asked to join the Smartpunk Stage of 2004 Vans Warped Tour where they continued to win the support of crowds everywhere they play. For fans of Fall Out Boy, and My Chemical Romance. Sadly, shortly after signing with No Milk Records ARR finally succumbed to the pressures of the road and disbanded. Mike went on to join the widley known band, Rookie of The Year . Bob and Dan have been rumored to be starting a dance revolution and Jordan went back to school in Arizona. However all is not lost, check out the Huge Discounts on ARR merchandise available exclusively from No Milk Records!

tbr.name: The Bank Robbers
tbr.title: [ NO MILK RECORDS | THE BANK ROBBERS ] Jackson / Howell, NJ Rock Band
bio: Childhood best friends from Central New Jersey came together in May of 1998 to form The Bank Robbers.

Fueled by raw passion, The Bank Robbers deliver honest, intense songs that bridge the gap between post-hardcore and rock. Intricate, powerful guitars, a solid rhythm section, and soaring vocals take The Bank Robbers a step above their counterparts. With a solid first release of strong melodies and intense musical composition under their belts (2003's The Pattern Reversed), The Bank Robbers have found their place and their sound.

On the evening of May 18, 2005, at The Continental Airlines Arena, Robert Nardone and Vinny Auletta were invited on stage to sing and perform I Still Havent Found What Im Looking For with the legendary U2. The very next day The Bank Robbers were contacted for interviews in a variety of print and digital publications. This larger than life experience was covered with a photo by ROLLING STONE MAGAZINE in the June 16, 2005 issue.

The following month The Bank Robbers entered Underground Sound Studios (Slipknot, Kittie, Biohazard) with producer Mike Turner, to begin tracking their sophomore album. The band was able to take their time, experiment, and capture a record that showcases the bands mature songwriting ability that focuses on structure and chorus, as well energy and passion. The band describes Tomorrow Belongs To Me as a record that listeners of all ages can relate to. It is compiled of a dynamic range of rock songs that showcase the bands love for many different styles of music.

After the sessions were wrapped, The Bank Robbers hit the road with a strenuous tour schedule hitting almost every state in the country. Fresh off a two-month tour of the US with Drive-Thru recording artists Socratic and House of Fools, the band made a stop in Austin, TX to perform at SXSW 2006. Their energetic set caused a frenzy of flash bulbs as photographers rushed to snap pictures of the band breaking glasses while swinging mic stands like baseball bats to create feedback during the bridge of their closing song.

With a solid two-month tour and a spot on the legendary SWSW under their belts, the band plans on touring nonstop throughout the US in the coming months in an attempt to not only gain new fans, but to also showcase their strict work ethic and convey their love for the new record.

hx.name: Halifax
hx.title: [ NO MILK RECORDS | HALIFAX ] A Writer's Reference, Thousand Oaks, CA
bio: Yeah, yeah. You know it already. Halifax can really party. Hell, even the old bag in the cubicle next to you probably knows them from their stint on The Real World Austin. But what’s decidedly more important is that the Thousand Oaks, California-reared quintet’s music translates. Just ask the million plus visitors to the band’s PureVolume page. But better proof lies with the band’s crackling debut album, The Inevitability of a Strange World, which finds frontman Mike Hunau, guitarists Chris Brandt and Adam Charles, bassist Doug Peyton and drummer Tommy Guindon at a distinct advantage over other booze-swilling, excess-extolling rising stars. Sure, many have tried through the years, but few bands have managed to bridge the great divide between rock, punk and metal with their hooks, hearts and hopes in tact quite the same way these electric warriors have.

More than mere trouble makers with guitars, Halifax are songcraft specialists with enough vision to merge the best of all possible approaches, which explains the group’s unique delegation of responsibilities to both Taking Back Sunday producer Lou Giordano and hard rock veteran Machine. “We loved working with Lou,” Hunau says. “His expertise was invaluable. But we wanted to put more ‘Oomph’ on the record, so Machine helped make it more aggressive. More in your face.” With that said, insistency abounds on The Inevitability of a Strange World. Be it the pop-meets-pummel charge of “Nightmare” or the irresistible, inventive first single, “Our Revolution.” The latter’s Mick Mars-themed riffs and rebellious “Hell yeah!” refrain qualify it as 7-Eleven parking lot music for the 21st Century. Says Mike, “It’s an homage to classic metal, and Motley Crue in particular.”

If Halifax’s melee-inspiring roar feels as woozily fun as it is proficient (few will be able to deny the exuberant crunch of “Under Fire,” for instance), it’s interesting to learn that the quintet’s influences vary from Nine Inch Nails to the Foo Fighters to reggae to Children of Bodom. “It’s almost like the music we listen to doesn’t necessarily shape our sound, as much as it helps to express what we are feeling,” says the singer.

From the coke-binge-gone-wrong theatrics of “Snow In Hollywood” to the stunning snarl of “Promise Me A Tragedy,” Hunau says most of the tunes in the Halifax songbook first germinate when he and Brandt collaborate. “It’s usually us coming up with a skeleton of a song and the lyrics and then we’re bringing it to the table and showing everyone what our version of it is,” he says. “And then everyone works on it together.” As frustrating as a rock democracy can be – Hunau says the sequencing of the disc was laborious due to disagreements – it’s this teamwork that eventually found the group a home on the infamous Drive-Thru Records label.

Rewind to 2003 and Halifax was just another in a myriad of unsigned but resolute indie outfits rolling the highways and byways of North America. Sharing van space, shitty hotel rooms, bodily aromas, Old Milwaukee and a collective dream in between crappy jobs in chain restaurants and landscaping, the group recorded and supported its initial EP, A Writer’s Reference. Within a year’s time, Halifax found itself among the lower echelon of the 2004 Warped Tour, but its reputation continued to grow. By early 2005, after establishing friendships with Drive-Thru founders Richard Reines and Stefanie Reines – and bowling them over during a New Jersey gig with The Early November – the label tweaked and reissued Reference. Appending an acoustic version of the band’s beloved “Sydney,” a track Hunau scribed in tribute to his late grandfather, Halifax continued touring and building its fanbase while concocting what would become The Inevitability of a Strange World.

When Mike, Chris, Adam, and Tommy landed in Austin, Texas for the renowned South By Southwest Music Festival last year, little did they know how a routine night in the world of rock & roll coupled with a few television cameras might sensationalize their image. “A lot of people who only know us from the TV will come to our shows and think we’re drunk off our asses or something,” Hunau chuckles. “But we didn’t do anything on the show that we don’t do normally. Bands go out drinking and get drunk and have fun and hang out with friends and chicks. It’s not like we’ll play with other bands and they’ll say, ‘Oh my god! Halifax is out of control.’ Yet anyone with an objective ear might garner such a notion in a positive sense by turning to The Inevitability of a Strange World. Take the contagious, exhilarating motion of “Better Than Sex,” for instance. Here, Brandt and Charles’ machine gun riffing escalates amid Hunau’s memorable, melodic intonations. Catapulted by the rhythmic drive of Peyton and Guindon, it’s evident that Halifax deserves the attention they’ve yielded so far.

If their intentions seem simple, they also seem pure. “No matter how shitty we’re feeling, there’s redemption when we go out and rock a crowd,” the singer acknowledges. “We definitely don’t just get up there and play our songs. We have a blast every night on stage.” Like we said, Halifax can party. Listen and live in the Strange World.

nhe.name: No Hollywood Ending
nhe.title: [ NO MILK RECORDS | NO HOLLYWOOD ENDING ] howell jackson NJ no milk records band
bio: No Hollywood Endings latest album will choke you at the throat and leave you spitting out verses that are reliable, quick, accurate and to the point, as guitarist and vocalist, CLC, describes their latest gutsy creation. Looking back on their first album, Its All a Nightmare released in 2004, No Hollywood Ending thought they knew what it took to bring their band to the main stage. At the time when it first came out, we were really excited about it and I think that we were on to something that nobody was doing at the time, says lead singer, Frank Osler. Now with their second full-length album, Everybodys Talking, the band has completely transformed. Over the years No Hollywood Ending faced some struggling encounters that challenged the band to remain as serious, focused, and united as they had hoped. With plans being made for their second album, they realized that if NHE was going to progress and grow as a band then they needed to crack down and focus on what was most important, and they did. I hate looking back. I just like moving forward, says CLC who is already getting amped about working on their third album with fellow band members, Osler, Ryan Lesinski (guitar), Steve Gotthelf (drums), and recent additions Kyle Mohr (synth/keys), and Joe Beninato (bass). With Its All a Nightmare, Osler feels that they were just a group of kids attempting to write good music, but now with Everybodys Talking, he is really proud of what they have accomplished and says that, The biggest difference is we learned how to write songs. We learned how to write them better and then finally, we all just stepped up and everything worked out perfectly. No Hollywood was able to deliver the hardcore sounds that frenzied fans expected of them, yet the band was still able to surprise them with songs that were creative and fresh. Sixteen Times is a big step for us. That is probably the best song we wrote, Osler says, whose lyrics withhold a catchier tone on this track. I know you like that, Confident, conceited, charming when needed.I know you like that,A boy so admired, handsome and desired. Were good at mixing it up, says Osler. We know how to write the hooks and then we know how to keep it heavy for the kids that want to hear the heavy shit we started out doing. The tracks on Everybodys Talking range from hand-clapping chants with more up-beat guitar sounds presented in ChaChaChastity, to the more hardcore songs with lyrics thatll slap you in the face as seen in Obituary Cover Girl. CLC says that, In this kind of music we just play for kids to go crazy. Theyre just there to have a good time for 40 minutes, go crazy as possible and drive home sweaty. Playing a ridiculous live show for the fans and having fun on stage is what NHE has been about since day one, says Osler. As for challenging themselves musically, NHE just might shock everyone with something highly unanticipated: a fifteen minute bonus track thats a massive medley of eclectic sound effects with an experimental flair, overlapping voice-overs, and lengthy, un-used riffs thatll make your head spin, as CLC describes his favorite part about the album. The name of the album is Everybodys Talking. Everybodys talking everywhere at all times. People are talking somewhere right nowin the next house, the next town, or the next country, says CLC as he explains the albums title which was inspired by the unexpected final track. Even producer, Mike Turner, got a big hit out of the idea. He let us try things, says Osler. The bottom line is, with music and lyrics like No Hollywood Endings slicing through the airwaves, theyre bound to make an impact on some level. I really dont know what to expect, says CLC regarding the future of the band. Just take the band as far as we can take it.

ro.name: Runaway Orange
ro.title: [ NO MILK RECORDS | RUNAWAY ORANGE ] Sewaren NJ pop rock band
bio: RUNAWAY ORANGE is a four piece from Woodbridge, NJ who writes energetic, melodic, catchy, emotional music about relationships, rights of passage, hardships, rising to the occasion, and just letting go. The band believes in living for the moment and takes advantage of every opportunity that comes their way. They have a huge influence from mainstream pop and have been compared to such bands as THIRD EYE BLIND, ALL AMERICAN REJECTS, and JIMMY EAT WORLD. RUNAWAY ORANGE have had the pleasure of touring the US several times as well as visiting Canada on the Drive-Thru Records Stage of the Vans Warped Tour. After finishing up the final touches on their debut full length, The Cutting Room, RUNAWAY ORANGE are anxious to get back on the road to tour the country and spread their unique blend of music to everyone.

sa.name: Sleepaway
sa.title: [ NO MILK RECORDS | SLEEPAWAY ] Buffalo rock band
bio: Emerging from Buffalo’s prestigious hardcore scene known for bands like Snapcase and Every Time I Die, SLEEPAWAY offers music from the other side of the spectrum. SLEEPAWAY combines shimmering guitar sounds with smooth vocals and piano melodies reminiscent of late 90’s alt rock like The Gin Blossoms and The Goo Goo Dolls. Formed in the Spring of 2005, with an average age of 19, SLEEPAWAY has been compared to the likes of indie giants Jimmy Eat World, and The Get Up Kids. Although these are monumental or even outlandish assertions, their pristine self titled debut clearly backs this up with a solid collection of 10 tracks each equally as strong as the next. Their love for vintage gear, alt rock, and meticulous musicianship are key elements driving this band to repeatedly perform and write each and every composition. Their hard work is being reinforced with praise from listeners of all ages and tastes including Gary Malibur (Steve Miller Band), Robby Takac (Goo Goo Dolls), Kevin Ratterman (Elliot), and even a Buffalo Bills cheerleader who features the band in her online profile. With a diverse array of fans, SLEEPAWAY is ready to show the world that Buffalo, NY has more to offer than hardcore, cold climate, and hot wings.

so.name: Socratic
so.title: [ NO MILK RECORDS | SOCRATIC ] Cranford, NJ rock band
bio: Cranford, New Jersey gives birth to the newest musical sensation that stands out in a state cluttered with hundreds of mediocre bands. SOCRATIC has quickly opened the eyes of many people. Following months of non-stop shows within New Jersey and it's surrounding states, SOCRATIC has rapidly grown a fan base within the region. They entered the studio to record their debut EP, It's Getting Late. Produced by Chris Badami (Fenix TX, Dillenger Escape Plan, The Starting Line, Midtown), the CD is a prime example of SOCRATIC's powerful guitars found in bands like Midtown with the classic guitar solos of Guns N Roses. Vocally, SOCRATIC offers amazingly catchy harmonies that have been compared to the likes of Jimmy Eat World, with rougher qualities of bands in the vein of Piebald. SOCRATIC knows how to write an impressive song and rock out accordingly. Their energetic live performances have earned them spots on bills with Hot Water Music, Thrice, the Get up Kids, and dates on the Drive-Thru Records Warped Tour stage. Fans of the genre are noticing this NJ band. A strong work ethic, and the love for the music, is driving them to the top.

to.name: Tourmaline
to.title: [ NO MILK RECORDS | TOURMALINE ] Verona, NJ Pop Band
bio: tour.ma.line ('turmu`leen) - [noun] 1. a mineral that is a complex borosilicate and hydroxide of aluminum containing iron, magnesium, calcium, lithium, and sodium; it is usually black but occurs in transparent colored forms that are used as gemstones 2. [band] a group hailing from the garden state, preparing to take the music world by storm. Carefully mixing an array of musical influences, from Jeff Buckley to Brand New, Elvis Costello to The Get Up Kids, The Beatles to Elliott Smith, and musically transcending several genres with their unique synth-driven melodies, powerful vocals, and heartfelt lyrics, Tourmaline is guaranteed to 'somehow just blow you away' (utterpunk.com). Matt Rauch, Ryan Baredes, Andrew Koes, Max Rauch, and Corey Zaloom formed Tourmaline early in 2004, and one year later they've found themselves signing to indie label No Milk Records (Socratic / Halifax), recording with producer Chris Bamini (The Early November / The Starting Line), having a track ('Blank') on a nationally distributed Drive Thru Records compilation, and sharing the stage with acts such as Head Automatica, Name Taken, The Beautiful Mistake, Punchline, and many more both in, and out of state. With a full length recently released on No Milk Records and various tours this summer, Tourmaline is showing that they are a musical force to be reckoned with. Combined with a relentless practicing schedule, frequent visits to the studio, powerful songwriting, and a ruthless drive to succeed, Tourmaline is quickly proving that they are indeed a precious gem in today's music world.

lf.name: Lady Fantastic
lf.title: [ NO MILK RECORDS | LADY FANTASTIC ] Hot Rod Hotel, Youngstown, OH
bio: This is what you get when you learn all your lessons the hard way. Write some songs, practice, record, book shows, buy a van, hit the road, then do it again. This is what we do. We never waited for that record deal or label interest to get started, this is going to be our life, and we will do it with or without help.

Our music is ever-evolving; influenced by our collective taste in music. Wed be lying if we said our style has never changed. Weve grown up as a band and as people, and our music reflects that. We call what we do progressive punk rock. Were not buying in to any specific genre or its uniform. Its more like calling in whats good about everything and cutting out the crap.

Hot Rod Hotel works kind of like a story. We wanted to write an album that was cohesive, but not necessarily a concept album. The idea: Make it feel like a walk through a hotel, and while passing each room, get the story that is going on inside. Musically, there is a lot going on; organs, strings, piano, and percussion all add to the mood and help create an atmosphere. Dual leading vocals help to define characters. Its heavy at times, and soft others.

releases.title: Sampler
facts: Recorded at Watchmen Studios | Lockport, NY
Produced, Enginered + Mixed by Doug White
description: This introduction to the band is only available in our online store and on tour. 3 songs that will make your heart pound with lust. This is just a sample of the powerful songwriting this band can offer. Beautifully raw compositions that border 90s rock and the new millenium of alternative. You need to hear to understand.

releases.coverAlt: Tourmaline, Strange Distress Calls CD/LP Cover
releases.title: Strange Distress Calls
facts: Recorded at Potrait Studios | Lincoln Park, NJ
Produced, Enginered + Mixed by Chris Badami
description: Carefully mixing an array of musical influences, from Jeff Buckley to Brand New, Elvis Costello to The Get Up Kids, The Beatles to Elliott Smith, and musically transcending several genres with their unique synth-driven melodies, powerful vocals, and heartfelt lyrics, Tourmaline is guaranteed to 'somehow just blow you away' (utterpunk.com). Powerful songwriting and strong choruses make it clear that Tourmaline is quickly proving that they are indeed a precious gem in today's music world.

releases.title: Friends & Family Sampler Vol.4
description: Traditionally handed out at Skate & Surf Festival every year, this is the first sampler that was given out at The Bamboozle which took the place of S&S. Drive-Thru Records, Rushmore Records, Eyeball Records, Doughmain Records, Evil Water Records, and RB Recordings all submitted artists. Bands include Tourmaline, The Bank Robbers, Halifax, No Hollywood Ending, Runaway Orange, Socratic, All Rights Reserved, Hidden In Plain View, Self Against City, Interference, InMemory, Vie Perdu, Eandi, Perfuma, Chasing Monroe, Silhouette, The Sideways, Que Cera, and Lucked Out.

releases.title: A Writer's Reference
facts: Recorded at Love Juice Labs | Riverside, CA
Produced, Enginered + Mixed by Rich "Beetlejuice" / Jeremy Swanson
description: This re-release includes enhanced footage as well as the bonus acoustic track of Sydney. Comes in digipak with brand new layout. Released in conjunction with Drive-Thru Records this EP has been converting listeners to fans instantly.

releases.coverAlt: All Rights Reserved, Remind Me To Burn THese Pages CD/EP Cover
releases.title: Remind Me To Burn These Pages
facts: Recorded at Nada Studios | New Windsor, NY
Produced, Enginered + Mixed by John Naclerio
description: This is the remastered version of the debut EP by ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. This re-issue of "Remind Me To Burn These Pages" includes new packaging and updated artwork! The five songs on this EP showcase the bands song writing ability to draw from a variety of influences. Music in the vein of Fall Out Boy, My Chemical Romance, and Boys Night Out.

releases.title: Friends & Family Sampler Vol.3
description: No Milk Records friends & Family Sampler vol. 3 includes artists from Drive-Thru Records, LLR Recordings, Radio Breakdown, Pumpkineater Records, and Genco Records. Artists include Halifax, No Hollywood Ending, The Bank Robbers, Runaway Orange, Jenoah, The Academy, Feeling Left Out, Style Over Substance, All Rights Reserved, Post Break Tragedy, Blue Star Drive, Surrounded By Lions, The Sideways, Perfuma, Kick Over The Traces, Lost But Found, The Grand Finals, and Gibbler.

releases.title: A Writer's Reference
facts: Recorded at Love Juice Labs | Riverside, CA
Produced, Enginered + Mixed by Rich "Beetlejuice' / Jeremy Swanson
description: Halifax delivers 6 tracks on their EP debut on No Milk Records. Fusing bright guitar hooks with memorable singing patterns, Halifax have been turning heads as they infect the ears of listeners throughout the country. A Writer's Reference shows the maturity of the band after time off for writing and regrouping with a new permanent lineup.

releases.title: It's All A Nightmare
facts: Recorded at MB Studios | Freehold, NJ
Produced, Enginered + Mixed by Mike Turner
description: No Hollywood Ending brought their basement experiments to life on the 2003 debut full length, It's All A Nightmare. Never holding creativity back, as you can tell while listening to the cd, with its rollercoaster like contents. From the beginning to the end you never know what to expect next.

releases.coverAlt: Runaway Orange, The Cutting Room CD/LP Cover
releases.title: The Cutting Room
facts: Recorded at Suburban Soul Studios | Highland Park, NJ
Produced, Enginered + Mixed by Ernest Ta / Charles Park
description: The Cutting Room is Runaway Orange's highly anticipated debut full length on No Milk Records. Amazing chorus', and vocal harmonies make this record a necessity to any CD collection. Eleven catchy rock ballads with punk influences make "The Cutting Room" the CD you will not want to take out of your stereo. This record is that good. For fans of Third Eye Blind, Jimmy Eat World, and All American Rejects.

releases.title: Friends & Family Sampler Vol.2
description: The second installment in the Friends & Family sampler series was released in 2003. Partnering labels include Wemake Records, Drive-Thru Records, and LLR Recordings. Bands on this disc include Runaway Orange, The Youth Ahead, The Bank Robbers, New Direxion, Socratic, Skyline, Signature Escape, Last Perfect Thing, Forevers End, English and the 40 ozers, August Premier, 504 Plan, Remember Maine, Afterproject, The Movielife, The Early November, The Years Gone By, All Rights Reserved, Reason To Believe, The New Haircut, Gibbler, and Lucked Out.

releases.coverAlt: The Bank Robbers, The Pattern Reversed CD/LP Cover
releases.title: The Pattern Reversed
facts: Recorded at MB Studios | Freehold, NJ
Produced, Enginered + Mixed by Mike Turner
description: The Pattern Reversed is 10 tracks filed with songs of love, and love lost. This energetic collection is heavy at times, yet comes full circle offering melodic ballads that reach deep into the human soul. Catchy choruses have been infecting listeners throughout the country.
This Cd has been recently re-releasesd with new artwork and an additional bonus trcak "The Way Things Fade".

releases.title: Friends & Family Sampler Vol.1
description: The first of many samplers to come devoted to raising awareness for artists on No Milk Records as well as other labels that we are friends with. With the aspiration to showcase addtitional unsigned bands who are working hard on their own, we include songs from these artists on the end of the disc. Bands on Friends & Family vol. 1 include The Bank Robbers, Dumbfounded, Forevers End, Runaway Orange, Finch, The Movielife, The Starting Line, Lucked Out, Day By Day, Gibbler, When Memories Die, A Day Late, Wayne's Basement, The Superspecs, Dakota Dream, and No Options.

releases.title: It's Getting Late
facts: Recorded at Portrait Studios | Lincoln Park, NJ
Produced, Enginered + Mixed by Chris Badami
description: Written when guitarist/singer Duane Okun was in the seventh grade, this EP is the digital history that laid the foundation for band to become the masterful musicians they are today. Socratic delivers these 6 tracks filled with ambition, energy, and the first examples of the bands ability to tell stories through lyric and song.
Including new artwork and enhanced archivale footage!
